nodes.name: Multi-shell Au self-template synthesis
nodes.procedure: The multi-shell Au spheres (MS-Au) were prepared by a facile self-template strategy, typically including the synthesis of Au-melamine colloidal templates and the rapid in-situ reduction process. The single-shell Au spheres (SS-Au) were also prepared (detailed in ESM Fig. S1).

nodes.name: Rh loading on multi-shell Au
nodes.procedure: After heating the mixture of multi-shell Au spheres and Rh salt in ethylene glycol, the metallic Rh nanoparticles were loaded into the porosity of multi-shell Au spheres. Thus, the bimetallic Au and Rh multi-shell structures, i.e., Rh/MS-Au, were prepared.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of pristine MS-Au exhibits well-crystallized metal Au phase (JCPDS 04-0784) with diffraction peaks at 2θ = 38.2°, 44.4°, 64.6°, and 77.5° corresponding to Au (111), (200), (220), and (311) planes. Rh/MS-Au shows Au peaks at same positions with no detectable Rh phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the pristine MS-Au exhibits a well-crystallized metal Au phase (JCPDS 04-0784) (Fig. 2(a)). The diffraction peaks at 2θ = 38.2°, 44.4°, 64.6°, and 77.5° correspond to the Au (111), (200), (220), and (311) crystalline planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Rh/MS-Au displays highly rough surfaces and spherical shape with outer diameter around 250 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figs. 2(b) and 2(c), Rh/MS-Au displays highly rough surfaces and spherical shape with an outer diameter around 250 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Rh/MS-Au possesses clear porous triple-shell structure assembled from nanoparticle structural units 5-10 nm. HRTEM shows lattice distances of 0.24 nm and 0.22 nm corresponding to Au(111) and Rh(111) planes, with ultrafine Rh nanoclusters 2-3 nm decorated on MS-Au interstices.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification TEM image in Fig. 2(d) reveals that Rh/MS-Au possesses a clear porous triple-shell structure. Close observation indicates that Rh/MS-Au is assembled from nanoparticle structural units with sizes ranging from 5 to 10 nm (Fig. 2(e)). As illustrated in the HRTEM image (Fig. 2(f)), the lattice distances of 0.24 and 0.22 nm correspond to the (111) plane of metal Au and (111) plane of metal Rh, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows obvious contrast between bright Au nanoparticle region and dark fringe-positioned Rh region.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image of Rh/MS-Au in Fig. 2(g) displays an obvious contrast between the bright Au nanoparticle region and the dark fringe-positioned Rh region due to the difference in atomic number.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Rh and Au elements in Rh/MS-Au.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images illustrates the uniform distribution of Rh and Au elements in Rh/MS-Au.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX line scanning across Rh/MS-Au shows sextuple signal peaks of Au and Rh, verifying hollow triple-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) line scanning profile (Figs. 2(h) and 2(i)) across Rh/MS-Au illustrated sextuple signal peaks of Au and Rh, further verifying the hollow triple-shell structure and the loading of Rh onto the inner and outer Au shells.

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh content in Rh/MS-Au determined as 0.54 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Rh content in Rh/MS-Au is determined to be 0.54 wt.% by the inductively coupled plasma (ICP) test, which is also consistent with the 0.58 wt.% in Rh/SS-Au and 0.65 wt.% in Rh/Au.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption shows specific surface area of 22.5 m²/g and rich porosity for Rh/MS-Au.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption–desorption isotherm in Fig. S5 in the ESM indicates the specific surface area of 22.5 m²·g⁻¹ and rich porosity for Rh/MS-Au.

nodes.characterization_summary: Au 4f peaks at 84.09 eV (4f7/2, up-shifted 0.32 eV vs MS-Au) and 88 eV (4f5/2) indicate electron transfer from Au to Rh. Rh 3d shows Rh⁰ at 307/312 eV and Rh³⁺ at 309/314 eV signals with blue shift from elemental Rh (307.60 eV), indicating electron transfer from Rh to Au and formation of coupled Au-Rh interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with MS-Au, the binding energy of Au 4f in Rh/MS-Au is up-shifted to 84.09 eV (by 0.32 eV), representing the electron transfer from Au to Rh. The Rh 3d3/2 binding energy shifts from 307.60 eV in elemental Rh to 307.34 eV in Rh/MS-Au by 0.26 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-Vis shows broad-range sunlight absorption for MS-Au, Rh/MS-Au, Rh/SS-Au; absorption increase 350-500 nm assigned to Rh LSPR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The UV–visible (UV–Vis) spectra recorded from an aqueous suspension containing MS-Au, Rh/MS-Au, Rh/SS-Au, and Rh/Au are shown in Fig. 3(d). The broad-range sunlight absorption properties were observed for MS-Au, Rh/MS-Au, and Rh/SS-Au.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ DRIFTS detects *CO₂ (1210 cm⁻¹), *CO (2080 cm⁻¹), *COOH (1745 cm⁻¹), *CHO_i (1080 cm⁻¹), *CH₃O (1106 cm⁻¹) intermediates on Rh/MS-Au surface confirming formyl pathway.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figs. 7(b) and 7(c), the absorption band characteristics of the surface-adsorbed *CO₂ and the typical *CO, *COOH, *CHO_i, and *CH₃O intermediates were detected at about 1210, 2080, 1745, 1080, and 1106 cm⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: j-t transient patterns show fast current response with on-off illumination cycles; Rh/MS-Au shows increased photocurrent vs MS-Au indicating enhanced photogenerated carrier generation, separation, and transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be observed that the on–off illumination cycles trigger fast current response for Rh/MS-Au and MS-Au samples. Obviously, the Rh/MS-Au sample with the Rh loading indicates an increase in the photocurrent.

nodes.characterization_summary: Photoluminescence spectra show Rh/MS-Au has higher emission intensity vs MS-Au, indicating more active charges and rapid transfer process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be observed that the Rh loading significantly promotes the emission signal intensity of Rh/MS-Au in comparison with the reference MS-Au.
